the effects of antibiotics on the environment are not yet fully understood, but that there is evidence of potential for adverse effects.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the antibiotic exposure caused a significant shift in community composition, with the greatest effect on the unacclimated communities.

the exposure of microbial communities from an oligo-trophic aquifer to concentrations of the antibiotic sulfamethyl-azole in the μg/L range, over 30 days, resulted in a decrease in the number of viable bacteria in previously unexposed communities and a decrease in sensitivity to sulfamethoxa-zole.
exposure to antibiotics can influence microbial community composition and function in the environment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
antibiotic concentrations in the μg-L(-1) range can have a significant impact on the composition and functioning of groundwater communities.
the effects of antibiotics on microbial communities in groundwater may not be as simple as previously thought.
the effects of antibiotics at concentrations of 2-3 log orders of magnitude below clinical levels are not negligible, and may have significant effects on groundwater microbial communities.
